articles.title: A working SOCKS5 proxy does not prove UDP support
articles.excerpt: A proxy test that only opens an HTTPS page cannot establish UDP support. The application may use TCP, fall back from HTTP/3, or apply its proxy setting to only part of its traffic. Diagnose the client…
articles.body: A proxy test that only opens an HTTPS page cannot establish UDP support. The application may use TCP, fall back from HTTP/3, or apply its proxy setting to only part of its traffic. Diagnose the client, relay and destination as separate parts of the path. UDP, QUIC and HTTP/3 have different jobs TCP supplies an ordered stream of bytes and handles retransmission when data is lost. UDP sends separate messages, called datagrams, without providing those delivery and ordering guarantees itself. Software using UDP decides how to deal with missing, late or duplicate messages. That makes UDP useful for applications with different priorities. A live voice application may prefer the next audio packet to a delayed replacement of an old one. A game can send frequent state updates.

articles.title: Lazy loading a product grid: which images should never get loading="lazy"
articles.excerpt: Adding loading="lazy" to every on a category page feels like free performance. It mostly is. The catch is the handful of images where it does the opposite of what you want, and on a store those are us…
articles.body: Adding loading="lazy" to every <img> on a category page feels like free performance. It mostly is. The catch is the handful of images where it does the opposite of what you want, and on a store those are usually the most important ones. Here's the short version of how I decide, image by image. The rule of thumb Lazy loading tells the browser: "don't fetch this until it's about to scroll into view." That's great for row 6 of a product grid. It's bad for anything the visitor sees the moment the page opens, because the browser now waits until layout is done to decide the image is "near the viewport" before it even starts the request. So the question for each image is simply: is it visible without scrolling on a typical screen? Yes: load it normally.

articles.title: Stop the Micromanagement: How to Fix a Broken Daily Stand-Up
articles.excerpt: If your Daily Stand-Up feels like a 15-minute micromanagement interrogation, stop immediately. You are doing it wrong. The Daily Scrum is absolutely not a status report for managers, stakeholders, or…
articles.body: If your Daily Stand-Up feels like a 15-minute micromanagement interrogation, stop immediately. You are doing it wrong. The Daily Scrum is absolutely not a status report for managers, stakeholders, or even the Scrum Master. It is a fast-paced, strategic alignment event built specifically by the developers, for the developers. Far too many teams treat their morning sync like a confessional. Engineers stand in a circle (or stare at a grid of Zoom squares) and justify their paychecks by listing everything they did yesterday. This reactive routine drains team energy and completely misses the point of agile frameworks. When executed correctly, this strict 15-minute daily ritual transforms reactive firefighting into proactive, high-velocity execution.

articles.title: How to auto-grade SQL exercises against a real SQLite database
articles.excerpt: If you teach SQL, you've probably tried grading by comparing a student's query with your own. It doesn't work, because two correct queries rarely look alike. All three of these answer the same questio…
articles.body: If you teach SQL, you've probably tried grading by comparing a student's query with your own. It doesn't work, because two correct queries rarely look alike. All three of these answer the same question, and all three pass the grader in this post: SELECT member , SUM ( days ) FROM loans GROUP BY member HAVING SUM ( days ) >= CAST ( readfile ( 'input' ) AS INTEGER ) ; SELECT member , total FROM ( SELECT member , SUM ( days ) AS total FROM loans GROUP BY member ) WHERE total >= CAST ( readfile ( 'input' ) AS INTEGER ) ; WITH totals AS ( SELECT member , SUM ( days ) AS total FROM loans GROUP BY member ) SELECT * FROM totals WHERE total >= 0 + readfile ( 'input' ) ORDER BY total DESC ; What does work is running each query against the same database and comparing the rows it returns.

articles.title: I built a workspace that reads my body, then asked it to leave me alone
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge. Most "smart" developer tools add things: another panel, another badge, another notification. I wanted the opposite. ZenDev is a develop…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Presage SmartSpectra SDK Challenge . What I Built Most "smart" developer tools add things: another panel, another badge, another notification. I wanted the opposite. ZenDev is a developer workspace that removes friction when I am calm and adds exactly one thing when I am not: a breath. It measures pulse, heart-rate variability, breathing and, when the SDK reports them, facial expressions and skin conductance through the Presage SmartSpectra SDK. It learns what calm looks like for me, then expresses everything else as a single relative number: a 0–100% load index. The interface cools and opens up when that number is low. When it climbs, lines loosen, the palette warms, and the bio-timeline records it. The part I care about most is the guardrail.

articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.title: Why did Starship Flight 15 booster abort 'chopsticks' landing catch? SpaceX still investigating (video)

articles.body: SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight. The goal: To land both the Super Heavy first stage and the Ship upper stage, for the first full Starship recovery — and the first complete recovery of an orbital launch system in history. The Super Heavy stage, called Booster 22, came back to Earth mere minutes after liftoff as planned.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier.

articles.title: Watch SpaceX will attempt its 1st-ever 'chopsticks' Starship landing catch of a rocket from orbit today (livestream)

articles.body: SpaceX plans to catch the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), and you can watch the action live. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen, however; SpaceX diverted Starship's Super Heavy booster to a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico 6.5 minutes after launch. (SpaceX said later that a guidance and navigaton issue during its descent triggered and automatic abort .

Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. articles.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX's Starship megarocket reached orbit today (Nov. 13) during its 15th test flight, but the company scrapped a plan to catch the vehicle's massive booster back at the launch site.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
